# Control map

This is an implemented control inventory, not a test-run report.
Review on changed standards, mechanisms, evidence or coverage. The
[registry](control-registry.json) owns these mappings; [engineering](engineering.md)
owns mandatory wording and [charter](charter.md) owns principles.

Automatic controls run in the common lane. Runtime controls act in the live system;
their tests cover only the stated cases. Manual controls require the named review
or probe. Implementation and evidence links do not assert a current execution or pass.

## Mechanisms and coverage

### C-PORTABLE — Portable regression lane (automatic)

Controller, HTTP adapter, setup and spectator regressions. Includes gameplay record validation and bounded evidence retention using synthetic observations. Passive planner/skill/supervisor composition, continuation and uncertainty are covered by real-component synthetic fixtures. Common command compiles Python, runs selected Ruff correctness diagnostics, Import Linter contracts, JavaScript syntax checks, Python tests and delayed-image viewer tests; markdown-it-py parses document links/images before contained file-target checks; diff whitespace is checked. Structured player tests exercise fixed HTTP transport, stable request fencing, exact archive images, semantic operations and SDK stdio text/structured/image framing.

Owner: maintainer. Trigger: each integration checkpoint and configured CI event.
Enforcement: Common command and opt-in local hook; main also requires the observed GitHub Actions controller check (app 15368) with strict freshness under active ruleset 25346774. Local hooks remain bypassable; dated hosted/probe evidence is in Enactive migration acceptance (original public-workflow results remain historical).
Failure response: Preserve failure output, fix the cause and rerun before claiming portable acceptance.

### C-RUNTIME — Live authority and input guards (runtime)

Single-controller mission dispatch and admission, original typed operation accounting, HTTP trust boundary, historical memory observer and spectator input freshness. One MissionRuntime accepts strict mission/7 through authenticated HTTP and bounded JSON CLI; old mission/2, mission/3, mission/4, mission/5 and mission/6 records and Stop-finish flags reject. One writer uses exact controller leases, final source/image preflight, durable intents and original root/child budgets. Controller/native fences reject stale, paused or competing input and retain unknown delivery without replay; admission counters exclude raw-command/Start races while independent Pause remains available. Registered launch retains the fixed child and paused menu. Creation/save/load requires owned transitions, provisional visible identity and canonical all-session adoption before maps, time or native memory facts. Verified normal exit retires only its exact pending input and unused capacity, preserving the unknown ACK. Normal finish uses every owned exit, retained historical source integrity and coherent objective Work as of its exact event; no native input. Its immutable report precedes terminal epoch/deadline checks, and Pause/expiry/crash cannot replay completion. Cached viewer status distinguishes historical memory, process samples, saved exit, reported completion, cleanup and actual mission phase; rendering grants no authority. Quiescent handoff/claim atomically retain actor history without input; bounded current-version successor packets cover unfinished Work. Separate linked readmission charges one Resume under original deadlines and exact source/Pause fences; history restores no consent. Typed item/count/inspection roots and one-observation activity polls share original phase/Work limits. Item quantity editing requires its exact returned count-opening transition; focus never auto-confirms. Trusted activity control captures validated terminal evidence before reconciliation persistence and checks fixed native expiry before publication. Cached SQLite aggregates distinguish retained operation requests and charged primitive dispositions from unmeasured model/tool/intervention costs. The observer separates current private activity from historical results and exposes bounded query-specific memory with explicit truncation/raw context. Known nondelivery retains costs without invalidating memory; freshness, scope and unknown effects still apply. A private unknown-dispatch candidate retains original root/actor/Pause/takeover/capacity custody. One bounded pre-Observe collection retains exact unclaimed retirement or correlated terminal evidence in existing records, without accepting it as current, clearing unknown effects or granting Resume. Delayed I/O cannot admit late evidence; collection misses remain ambiguous. Ledger9 uses one closed 32768-byte typed EffectReconciliation envelope for delivery, lifecycle and owned exit. Write/reopen correlate basis semantics with independent original dispatch receipts, actor/root/Work/epoch, source IDs and collection clocks; old ledger/effect shapes reject. Framed late results consume original reserved capacity before diagnostic Observe. Explicit reconciliation needs current fresh paused evidence and does not rewrite the unknown ACK/charge. Separate normal-play recovery readmission charges one Resume; navigation retains its original goal/Work/root, first game anchor and cumulative limits. Pending continuation fences competing roots/handoff; unknown Resume and unsupported ownership stop. Historical or orphan proof restores no private consent. Aged lifecycle Resume and owned quit confirmation refresh the exact guarded checkpoint inside the operation under original child/root/mission deadlines. Resume records source lineage before a lease exists; typed exit revalidation links the immutable interpretation to the dispatched source at write/reopen and orphan proof checks, requiring exact PNG rather than native-state equivalence. Local malformed lifecycle confirmation returns blocked before dispatch without renewing the original phase; corrected requests retain full source/Pause/image/deadline checks. Known game-time exhaustion gates every input lane and revokes authority after settlement; software maximum eight days, default twelve hours, no cleanup exemption. Eligible internally inconsistent skill source metadata returns blocked before refresh, phase mutation or primitive admission only after applicable existing authority/ownership/budget and native-state/image fences; original deadlines and consent remain unchanged. A new corrected request ID traverses every normal guard; no generic evidence-error exemption or compatibility path exists. The pure canonical client producer derives opaque metadata/root bindings from explicitly selected retained context and semantic intent, rejects unsupported scope combinations locally, and reuses current schema validation. It performs no I/O or authority grant; live guards remain authoritative. Semantic dismissal selects one category-specific registered action (TEXT.QUIT, UILIST.QUIT, WORLDGEN_CONFIRM.QUIT or ordinary QUIT), blocks if absent without alias substitution, and returns partial without answering a later prompt.

Owner: controller and viewer maintainer. Trigger: every relevant request, observation and image decode.
Enforcement: Implemented at runtime; regression execution is C-PORTABLE. Source references alone establish no behavioral pass.
Failure response: Reject or freeze further dispatch; expose error and reconcile by observation before explicit resume.

### C-NATIVE — Native build and real-game acceptance (manual)

Changed native/input/rendering/protocol/compiler/source-pin behavior and new support claims. Follow native acceptance probes, inspect actual game/spectator frames and record dated outcomes, environment, candidate and hashes.

Owner: integration maintainer; lead verifies evidence. Trigger: relevant native boundary change or new native release/support claim.
Enforcement: Required by S-PROTOCOL/S-DELIVERY and release review; manual, outside the portable gate. Permission readiness before ordinary campaign input also requires S-OPS's [live permission preflight](operator-permissions.md#preflight-for-every-campaign) from the actual designated player and exact entry point. Retain enabled project-layer evidence, rule decisions and live results separately. Repeated per-action review fails permission readiness even if every request is approved; resolve it before ordinary play. This is a manual activation check; prefix matching does not prove runtime loading.
Failure response: Retain failed/unknown probes, block the affected claim and repair or document the supported limit.

### C-BOUNDARY — Architectural dependency contracts (automatic)

Declared controller and server dependency boundaries, including indirect imports through harness modules. All passive gameplay modules, including supervision, must not import controller, HTTP, CLI or process/build tooling. Shared movement policy cannot depend on consumers, clock, filesystem or transport. Import Linter uses the pyproject.toml forbidden contracts: controller cannot depend on server, CLI, declared network modules or build tooling; server cannot depend on CLI/tools; CLI may compose both. Fourth forbidden contract isolates harness.movement; negative import fixtures exercise it.

Owner: harness maintainer. Trigger: common command; architecture changes require rule review.
Enforcement: Common command runs the real lint-imports executable and propagates failure; temporary source fixtures exercise allowed composition and direct/indirect forbidden imports.
Failure response: Remove reversed dependency or review the boundary and checker together before accepting changed architecture.

### C-REVIEW — Design and independent change review (manual)

Consequential designs, implementation, tests, delegation and exceptions. Lead owns design/integration and verifies returned evidence; at most two workers use separate project-local worktrees and named disjoint paths, with shared runtime serialized; fresh-context review assesses contracts, risk and maintainability before acceptance. Review new or expanded custom infrastructure across code/docs/workflow/controls against S-CODE: name the existing option, unmet gap, smallest scope, owner/cost and retirement trigger; reject unjustified duplication. Before publication, inspect explicit Git author/committer identities and all new commit messages, including co-author trailers, under S-WORK. Use repository-local Git identity configuration. Before merging a PR whose Issue completion awaits merged-main validation, read gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences, require an empty list and re-read after removing references. Prose negation is not a parser control; use GitHub computed data, no custom keyword parser. For source-dependent consequential claims, inspect executable predicates, caller cadence, units and defaults against actual outcomes; preserve mistaken rationale and which actions preceded correction. For changed native boundaries, compare synthetic category/action/row/transition assumptions with the pinned producer and retained visible frames; reject fictional UI labels used to arm control state. Reuse the existing regression/native lanes; do not infer native support from passing mocks.

Owner: lead; reviewer supplies independent findings. Trigger: significant change, new boundary/guarantee/dependency or integration checkpoint.
Enforcement: Required by S-AGENT and the GitHub work/PR workflow; independent agent review is manually recorded, not an independent GitHub human approval. Hosted enforcement is recorded separately in acceptance.
Failure response: Resolve material findings or record scoped owner/reason/revisit exception; after two unsuccessful worker repairs lead takes back the work.

### C-RELEASE — Exact candidate and evidence review (manual)

Checkpoint/release scope, source provenance and validation lanes. Inspect staged diff and candidate identity, run common checks against exact candidate, review pins/open exceptions and require relevant native probes for affected claims. Git owns tracked-source identity: commit before native acceptance and use commit/tree/diff/PR; hash external artifacts instead of maintaining per-source history.

Owner: lead or releasing maintainer. Trigger: checkpoint, release or support claim.
Enforcement: Main requires a PR, the Actions-bound controller check and resolved conversations; no force-push/deletion or configured bypass. Lead still owns native/release acceptance. Zero required human approvals is an explicit single-account limit; agent review is not human approval.
Failure response: Hold the affected acceptance/release claim until failed or unexecuted required lanes are resolved or scope is explicitly reduced.

Evidence / implementation: [docs/setup.md#evidence-and-releases](../docs/setup.md#evidence-and-releases), [docs/engineering.md](../docs/engineering.md), [docs/runbook.md#native-acceptance-lane](../docs/runbook.md#native-acceptance-lane), [native/upstream.json](../native/upstream.json), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-18-waypoint-readiness.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-18-waypoint-readiness.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-18-enactive-migration.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-18-enactive-migration.md).

Coverage gap: Working-tree hooks do not prove a partially staged candidate. Hosted source/check enforcement does not establish native gameplay, semantic review or release authority. No tag or release automation is installed; administrators can later change rules. GitHub requires association with an opened PR, not use of its merge button; a passing PR head can be pushed and recognized as merged. A required-PR rejection probe needs a CI-passing commit with no PR.

Lifecycle: active. Rationale: none recorded. Replacement: none.

### C-MAINTENANCE — Drift, recovery and retention review (manual)

Active guidance, dependency/research freshness, failure evidence and project-owned cleanup. Review active guidance/visuals, controls and dependencies on changed behavior/failure/release/resumption and within recorded periodic dates. Record findings, effectiveness, cost and follow-up in registry with dated evidence; promote repeated defects into tests or revise/retire controls. C-GOVERNANCE detects elapsed due dates when invoked. Revisit custom tools/processes and rejected reuse choices on upstream support/capability, requirement, defect or upkeep changes; replace or retire duplication under the existing owner/record.

Owner: maintainer; lead tracks active work. Trigger: behavior/control failure, release, resumed work or active-development review interval.
Enforcement: Manual requirements under S-OPS/S-AGENT/S-DOCS/S-EVIDENCE, with registry fields, references and overdue dates enforced by C-GOVERNANCE in the common lane.
Failure response: Record specific owner and next action, repair inaccurate guidance and preserve unresolved failures; never delete saves as routine cleanup.

### C-VISUAL — Rendered visual documentation (automatic)

Mermaid sources and generated SVGs in docs/diagrams. Pinned local Mermaid CLI renders every source in a headless project-local browser. Hash receipt covers sources, config, wrapper, package lock and tracked SVGs; title/description and root SVG ID are required. Explicit --write regenerates; normal checks leave tracked files unchanged.

Owner: documentation maintainer. Trigger: common command; source, renderer configuration or dependency changes require rendered review.
Enforcement: Common command fails on renderer errors, missing title/description/ID or changed input/output receipts; negative fixtures include a real parse failure. No global installation or automatic fetch.
Failure response: Fix syntax or missing setup; regenerate stale output and inspect the rendered result. Never call a denied browser launch a passed check. Resolve semantic/readability findings through C-USABILITY/C-REVIEW.

Evidence / implementation: [tools/diagrams.py](../tools/diagrams.py), [tests/test_diagrams.py](../tests/test_diagrams.py), [docs/diagrams/rendered.json](../docs/diagrams/rendered.json), [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md), [docs/overview.md](../docs/overview.md), [package.json](../package.json), [package-lock.json](../package-lock.json), [.puppeteerrc.cjs](../.puppeteerrc.cjs), [docs/decisions/004-documentation-controls.md](../docs/decisions/004-documentation-controls.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-recovery-evaluation.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-recovery-evaluation.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-passive-supervisor.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-passive-supervisor.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-18-integrated-player.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-18-integrated-player.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-18-walk-reassessment.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-18-walk-reassessment.md).

Coverage gap: Receipt freshness is not cross-host byte equality or proof against deliberate falsification. Rendering and SVG metadata do not prove meaning, accessibility for every reader or readable layout. Human rendered inspection is required. Ubuntu 24.04 CI was exercised with a scoped runner Chrome sandbox profile; other Linux hosts remain unverified.

Lifecycle: active. Rationale: Required to keep user-facing visual explanations reviewable and synchronized.. Replacement: none.

## Interpreting results

Run `.venv/bin/python tools/check.py` for the portable lane; update this map with
`.venv/bin/python tools/governance.py --write`. The latter validates before writing and
does not run gameplay. Dated executions belong in [acceptance](acceptance/2026-10-17-mvp.md)
and [work](work.md), with exact candidate, failures and unexecuted lanes.
